title: Web Crypto
lede: Web Crypto here is compile-time dispatched: the algorithm argument must be a string literal or an object literal with a literal name: — a variable holding the name is a compile error, and bare crypto.subtle as a value is unsupported. Operational failures throw synchronously at the call site rather than rejecting the returned promise, though await/.then/.catch/.finally all work on the settled result. crypto.subtle.* delegates to a native backend picked with -crypto (OpenSSL libcrypto by default, Apple CommonCrypto on macOS); getRandomValues and randomUUID need only a CSPRNG and no external library.

entries.name: crypto.getRandomValues(view)
entries.description: Fills an integer TypedArray's (or whole ArrayBuffer's) bytes in place from the in-house CSPRNG — arc4random_buf on macOS/BSD, getrandom() on Linux — and returns the same view. The spec's 65,536-byte quota is enforced (an oversize view throws QuotaExceededError), and a float TypedArray is a compile-time rejection matching the spec's TypeMismatchError. The legacy plain number[] form still works, writing one random byte value (0–255) per element.

params.name: view
params.desc: The buffer to fill in place.

differences: A whole `ArrayBuffer` is accepted as a deliberate extension (real JS throws `TypeMismatchError` — only integer TypedArrays are spec-legal).

entries.name: crypto.randomUUID()
entries.description: Returns a standard RFC 4122 version-4 UUID string. The version nibble (4) and variant nibble (one of 8/9/a/b) are fixed by the spec's bit layout; the rest is CSPRNG-random.
entries.snippet:
const id1: string = crypto.randomUUID()
const id2: string = crypto.randomUUID()

entries.name: crypto.subtle.digest(algo, data)
entries.signature: digest(algo: string | { name: string }, data: TypedArray | ArrayBuffer): Promise<ArrayBuffer>
entries.description: Hashes a TypedArray or ArrayBuffer with SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512, returning a Promise<ArrayBuffer>. Known-answer-tested against the NIST vectors on both backends.
entries.snippet: const sha256 = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", data))
differences: The algorithm argument must be a string literal or an object literal with a literal `name:` (a variable holding the name is a compile error — compile-time dispatch)
Results return as settled task promises: `await`/`.then`/`.catch`/`.finally` all work, but operational failures throw synchronously at the call site instead of rejecting the promise
Bare `crypto.subtle` as a value (e.g. `const s = crypto.subtle`) is not supported — methods must be called directly

entries.name: crypto.subtle.encrypt / .decrypt
entries.signature: encrypt(algo, key: CryptoKey, data): Promise<ArrayBuffer>; decrypt(algo, key: CryptoKey, data): Promise<ArrayBuffer>
entries.description: AES-GCM (iv, optional additionalData, optional tagLength default 128; auth failure → OperationError), AES-CBC (iv, PKCS#7), and RSA-OAEP (public encrypts / private decrypts, optional label), each returning a Promise<ArrayBuffer>.

params.name: algo
params.desc: Algorithm literal with its parameters (iv, label, …).

entries.snippet:
const ct = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: "AES-GCM", iv: iv }, aesKey, secret)
const pt = await crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: "AES-GCM", iv: iv }, aesKey, ct)
differences: On `-crypto=commoncrypto` only: a non-empty RSA-OAEP `label` throws `NotSupportedError` (SecKey has no label parameter)
The algorithm argument must be a string literal or an object literal with a literal `name:` (a variable holding the name is a compile error — compile-time dispatch)
Results return as settled task promises: `await`/`.then`/`.catch`/`.finally` all work, but operational failures throw synchronously at the call site instead of rejecting the promise
Bare `crypto.subtle` as a value (e.g. `const s = crypto.subtle`) is not supported — methods must be called directly

entries.name: crypto.subtle.sign / .verify
entries.signature: sign(algo, key: CryptoKey, data): Promise<ArrayBuffer>; verify(algo, key: CryptoKey, sig, data): Promise<boolean>
entries.description: HMAC (constant-time verify), RSA-PSS (runtime saltLength), and ECDSA over P-256/P-384/P-521 (per-call literal hash, raw r‖s signatures). sign returns Promise<ArrayBuffer>, verify returns Promise<boolean>.

params.name: data
params.desc: Message bytes (verify also takes the signature).

returns.desc: Signature bytes, or a verification result.

entries.snippet:
const sig = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.sign("HMAC", hmacKey, msg))
console.log(await crypto.subtle.verify("HMAC", hmacKey, sig, msg)) // true
differences: On `-crypto=commoncrypto` only: RSA-PSS `saltLength` must equal the hash length or `NotSupportedError` is thrown (SecKey fixes salt = digest size)
The algorithm argument must be a string literal or an object literal with a literal `name:` (a variable holding the name is a compile error — compile-time dispatch)
Results return as settled task promises: `await`/`.then`/`.catch`/`.finally` all work, but operational failures throw synchronously at the call site instead of rejecting the promise
Bare `crypto.subtle` as a value (e.g. `const s = crypto.subtle`) is not supported — methods must be called directly

entries.name: crypto.subtle.generateKey
entries.signature: generateKey(algo, extractable: boolean, usages: string[]): Promise<CryptoKey | CryptoKeyPair>
entries.description: Generates AES-GCM/AES-CBC (length:), HMAC (hash:, spec-default length), RSA-OAEP/RSA-PSS (modulusLength, hash) and ECDSA (namedCurve) keys, returning a Promise<CryptoKey> or a Promise<CryptoKeyPair> (.publicKey/.privateKey). Usages are enforced and spec-split across a key pair.

params.name: algo
params.desc: Algorithm literal with its key parameters.

params.name: extractable
params.desc: Whether the key may be exported.

returns.desc: The generated key or key pair.

entries.snippet:
const aesKey = await crypto.subtle.generateKey(
    { name: "AES-GCM", length: 256 }, false, ["encrypt", "decrypt"])
differences: `publicExponent` restricted to 65537 (the literal `new Uint8Array([1, 0, 1])`, or omit it)
The algorithm argument must be a string literal or an object literal with a literal `name:` (a variable holding the name is a compile error — compile-time dispatch)
Results return as settled task promises: `await`/`.then`/`.catch`/`.finally` all work, but operational failures throw synchronously at the call site instead of rejecting the promise
Bare `crypto.subtle` as a value (e.g. `const s = crypto.subtle`) is not supported — methods must be called directly

entries.name: crypto.subtle.importKey / .exportKey
entries.signature: importKey(format, keyData, algo, extractable, usages): Promise<CryptoKey>; exportKey(format, key): Promise<ArrayBuffer | Map<string,string>>
entries.description: raw (AES/HMAC bytes; EC public uncompressed points both ways), pkcs8 (private), spki (public), and jwk (oct/RSA/EC; object literal or Map in, Map out). Kind/format mismatches and non-extractable export throw InvalidAccessError.

returns.desc: A CryptoKey, or exported bytes / a JWK Map.

differences: `jwk` is surfaced as a `Map<string,string>` (this compiler has no dynamic object model), key-material members only (`kty`/`k`/`crv`/`n`/`e`/`d`/…) — no `key_ops`/`ext`/`alg` members; import never validates `kty`
`CryptoKey.algorithm`/`.usages` property reads not implemented (`.type`/`.extractable` work)
`raw` export of a non-EC asymmetric key isn't rejected (yields the stored DER)
The algorithm argument must be a string literal or an object literal with a literal `name:` (a variable holding the name is a compile error — compile-time dispatch)
Results return as settled task promises: `await`/`.then`/`.catch`/`.finally` all work, but operational failures throw synchronously at the call site instead of rejecting the promise
Bare `crypto.subtle` as a value (e.g. `const s = crypto.subtle`) is not supported — methods must be called directly

entries.name: crypto.subtle.deriveKey / .deriveBits
entries.signature: deriveKey(algo, baseKey, derivedAlgo, extractable, usages): Promise<CryptoKey>; deriveBits(algo, baseKey, length): Promise<ArrayBuffer>
entries.description: PBKDF2 (salt, iterations, literal hash) and HKDF (salt, optional info, literal hash). deriveBits returns a Promise<ArrayBuffer>; deriveKey produces an AES-GCM/AES-CBC/HMAC Promise<CryptoKey>. Known-answer-tested against RFC 6070/5869 on both backends.

returns.desc: The derived key or raw bits.

differences: The spec's extractable=false requirement on PBKDF2/HKDF base keys is not enforced
The algorithm argument must be a string literal or an object literal with a literal `name:` (a variable holding the name is a compile error — compile-time dispatch)
Results return as settled task promises: `await`/`.then`/`.catch`/`.finally` all work, but operational failures throw synchronously at the call site instead of rejecting the promise
Bare `crypto.subtle` as a value (e.g. `const s = crypto.subtle`) is not supported — methods must be called directly

entries.name: crypto.createHash / createHmac / hash / getHashes
entries.signature: createHash(algorithm, options?): Hash; createHmac(algorithm, key): Hmac; hash(algorithm, data, outputEncoding?): string
entries.description: Node's Hash and Hmac objects: .update(data) (chainable, string or bytes), .digest(encoding?) and Hash's .copy(). Every digest the crypto backend has is available, including shake128/shake256 with an outputLength. Validation and errors are Node's: a second digest throws ERR_CRYPTO_HASH_FINALIZED, and an unknown algorithm throws 'Digest method not supported'.

returns.desc: A digest handle, or the one-shot digest.

differences: On -crypto=commoncrypto only md5, sha1, sha224, sha256, sha384 and sha512 exist; SHAKE, SHA-3, SHA-512/t, RIPEMD-160 and BLAKE2 throw 'Digest method not supported'.

entries.name: crypto.createCipheriv / createDecipheriv / getCiphers
entries.signature: createCipheriv(algorithm, key, iv, options?): Cipheriv; createDecipheriv(algorithm, key, iv, options?): Decipheriv
entries.description: Symmetric encryption with any cipher the backend has. update/final, setAutoPadding, and setAAD, getAuthTag and setAuthTag for AEAD modes such as GCM. A wrong key or IV length, a bad final block, and a failed authentication throw the errors Node throws.
differences: On -crypto=commoncrypto only AES-128/192/256 in CBC, ECB, CTR and GCM exist; other ciphers throw ERR_CRYPTO_UNKNOWN_CIPHER.

entries.name: crypto.pbkdf2 / scrypt / hkdf (+ Sync)
entries.signature: pbkdf2(password, salt, iterations, keylen, digest, callback); scrypt(password, salt, keylen, options?, callback); hkdf(digest, ikm, salt, info, keylen, callback)
entries.description: Key derivation. The Sync forms return a Buffer (hkdfSync an ArrayBuffer); the callback forms run on the thread pool and call back with (err, key), as Node's do.

returns.desc: The derived key, or nothing for the callback form.

differences: On -crypto=commoncrypto the digests are the six createHash has there.

entries.name: crypto.randomBytes / randomFill / randomInt / timingSafeEqual / constants
entries.signature: randomBytes(size, callback?); randomFill(buf, offset?, size?, callback); randomInt(min?, max, callback?); timingSafeEqual(a, b)
entries.description: CSPRNG bytes and integers. randomBytes and randomFill fill on the thread pool when given a callback; randomInt is Node's rejection-sampling draw. timingSafeEqual compares in constant time and throws Node's RangeError on a length mismatch. constants is Node's table.

returns.desc: Random bytes, a random integer, or the comparison.

entries.snippet:
const token = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex')
const die = crypto.randomInt(1, 7)

entries.name: crypto.generateKeyPair / createSign / createVerify / sign / verify
entries.signature: generateKeyPair(type, options, callback); generateKeyPairSync(type, options): { publicKey, privateKey }; sign(algorithm, data, key); verify(algorithm, data, key, signature)
entries.description: rsa, ec, ed25519 and x25519 key pairs as PEM strings, and signatures over PEM keys: Sign/Verify streams and the one-shot sign/verify (null algorithm for Ed25519). The callback form of generateKeyPair runs on the thread pool.

returns.type: { publicKey: string, privateKey: string } | Buffer | boolean
returns.desc: A PEM key pair, a signature, or the verification.

differences: Keys are PEM strings only: generateKeyPair needs publicKeyEncoding { type: 'spki', format: 'pem' } and privateKeyEncoding { type: 'pkcs8', format: 'pem' }. There are no KeyObject results, no pkcs1/sec1/der formats, and no cipher/passphrase.
An encrypted PEM key ({ key, passphrase }) is not decrypted.
On -crypto=commoncrypto: RSA keys of 1024 bits or more with exponent 65537, and EC keys on P-256/P-384/P-521 only.
